nodes.label: ls
nodes.description: Lists directory contents and displays file and directory metadata depending on options.

nodes.label: cd
nodes.description: Changes the current working directory to a specified path.

nodes.label: pwd
nodes.description: Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.

nodes.label: -a
nodes.description: Includes all entries, even those that are normally hidden, such as dotfiles or user processes.

nodes.label: -A
nodes.description: Includes all entries except for implied . and .. directories.

nodes.label: -l
nodes.description: Displays information in a long listing format, including permissions, owner, group, size, and timestamp.

nodes.label: -r
nodes.description: Performs the operation recursively on subdirectories and their contents.

nodes.label: -R
nodes.description: Recursively processes all subdirectories. Same effect as -r in many commands.

nodes.label: -f
nodes.description: Forces the operation to continue without prompts, even on errors or overwrites.

nodes.label: -i
nodes.description: Asks for confirmation before performing actions like deletions or overwrites.

nodes.label: -v
nodes.description: Enables verbose output, displaying what the command is doing.

nodes.label: -p
nodes.description: Preserves attributes (like timestamps, permissions) or creates parent directories as needed.

nodes.label: -h
nodes.description: Displays file sizes in human-readable format (e.g. 1K, 234M, 2G).

nodes.label: -n
nodes.description: Suppresses the trailing newline (e.g. in echo) or prevents overwriting existing files (in cp or mv).

nodes.label: -e
nodes.description: Enables interpretation of backslash escape sequences (e.g. \n, \t) in strings.

nodes.label: -d
nodes.description: Treats directories as files and avoids listing their contents.

nodes.label: -m
nodes.description: Displays entries separated by commas instead of in columns or lines.

nodes.label: -t
nodes.description: Sorts results by modification time, newest files first.

nodes.label: -S
nodes.description: Sorts entries by file size, largest first.
Forces output to be listed one item per line.

nodes.label: -x
nodes.description: Displays entries horizontally across the screen rather than in columns.

nodes.label: -q
nodes.description: Replaces non-printable characters in filenames with question marks.

nodes.label: --help
nodes.description: Displays a short help text and exits. Common to most CLI tools.

nodes.label: --version
nodes.description: Displays version information and exits. Standard across GNU/Linux tools.

nodes.label: --hide
nodes.description: Excludes entries matching a specified pattern from output.

nodes.label: --hyperlink
nodes.description: Adds terminal hyperlink metadata to file entries, if supported by terminal.

nodes.label: --color
nodes.description: Colorizes the output; accepts values like 'auto', 'always', or 'never'.

nodes.label: File
nodes.description: A file is a data object stored in the filesystem. It can contain text, binary data, or be executable.

nodes.label: Directory
nodes.description: A directory is a container that holds files and other directories, forming the file hierarchy.

nodes.label: Symbolic Link
nodes.description: A symbolic link is a reference that points to another file or directory.

nodes.label: Hidden File
nodes.description: A hidden file is a file or directory that begins with a dot (.) and is not shown by default.

nodes.label: Exit Code
nodes.description: The exit code is a numeric value returned by a process to indicate success or failure.

nodes.label: if
nodes.description: Evaluates a condition and executes a block of code if the condition is true.

nodes.label: for
nodes.description: Iterates over a list or sequence of values and runs the code block for each item.

nodes.label: while
nodes.description: Executes a block of code repeatedly as long as the condition is true.

nodes.label: Variable Assignment
nodes.description: Stores a value in a shell variable for reuse.

nodes.label: Redirection
nodes.description: Redirects standard output or error to a file or another stream.

nodes.label: then
nodes.description: Marks the beginning of a code block that should execute if a condition is true.

nodes.label: else
nodes.description: Defines the code block to execute when the if-condition is false.

nodes.label: do
nodes.description: Marks the beginning of a loop body for for-, while-, or until-loops.

nodes.label: done
nodes.description: Marks the end of a loop body for for-, while-, or until-loops.

nodes.label: case
nodes.description: Performs multi-branch selection based on pattern matching.

nodes.label: Function
nodes.description: Defines a reusable block of code that can be called by name.

nodes.label: return
nodes.description: Exits a function and optionally returns a numeric status code.

nodes.label: read
nodes.description: Reads a line of input from standard input and stores it in a variable.

nodes.label: test
nodes.description: Evaluates expressions and returns a success or failure exit status.

nodes.label: esac
nodes.description: Marks the end of a case statement.

nodes.label: -eq
nodes.description: Numeric equality check. Returns true if the two numbers are equal. Only valid within test expressions like [ ... ] or test.

nodes.label: -ne
nodes.description: Numeric inequality check. Returns true if the numbers are not equal. Only valid within test expressions.

nodes.label: -lt
nodes.description: Numeric less-than comparison. Only usable inside test expressions.

nodes.label: -le
nodes.description: Numeric less-than-or-equal comparison inside test conditions.

nodes.label: -gt
nodes.description: Numeric greater-than comparison inside test expressions.

nodes.label: -ge
nodes.description: Numeric greater-than-or-equal comparison. Must be used in test or [ ].
Checks if two strings are equal. Only valid in [ ] or [[ ]].
Checks if two strings are not equal. Only usable in test contexts.

nodes.label: -z
nodes.description: Returns true if the string is empty. Only used inside [ ] or test.

nodes.label: -n
nodes.description: Returns true if the string is not empty. Valid only in test expressions.
